history.summary: Built by the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) and inaugurated in 1998 by Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Constructed entirely of interlocking stone per Vedic Shilpa Shastra with no cement or concrete, using pink sandstone from Bansipahadpur (Rajasthan) and Ambaji/Makrana marble; it has seven shikhars, 108 intricately carved pillars and 93 torans. The central shrine houses marble murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Gunatitanand Swami and Gopalanand Swami; other shrines hold a Panchdhatu Harikrishna Maharaj and Ghanshyam Maharaj. Coordinates are approximate (Kalawad Road centroid) - no precise POI geocode for the mandir was returned.

name: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Rajkot
town_description: Rajkot is the largest city in Gujarat's Saurashtra region and a former princely state capital; Mahatma Gandhi spent part of his early life here, and it is now a major commercial and industrial hub.

travel.airport: Hirasar Rajkot International Airport (~36 km) is the main airport.
travel.railway: Rajkot Junction is ~4 km from the mandir (per Trawell.in).
travel.road: On Kalawad Road near Mahila College, Vaishali Nagar (Rajkot 360007); Premvati canteen on the premises serves affordable Gujarati food.

visitor_information.best_time: Year-round; evenings or early mornings for aarti with fewer crowds (per Wanderlog).
visitor_information.opening_hours: 7:30-10:15 AM, 11:15 AM-12:00 noon, 4:00-6:00 PM, 7:00-8:15 PM (per indiamapped.com - verify).
